title: Kube scheduler backpressure + CNI churn investigation notes
content:
Summary:
Seen elevated PodStartup latency and a cluster-wide increase in Pending pods for ~35 minutes on 2025-11-02 03:14-03:49 UTC. Symptoms correlated with bursts of CNI programming retries and high conntrack churn on a subset of GPU worker nodes. The kube-scheduler logs show repeated predicate evaluation stalls and lock contention while trying to bind pods to nodes.

Impact:
- ~18% of new pods scheduled during window entered Pending > 30s (p95 ~ 120s).
- Several latency-sensitive workers saw timeouts and client retries.
- No etcd failure or API-server 5xx observed.

How detected / signals:
- Alert: SRE-POD-STARTUP-P95 exceeded threshold (pager triggered).
- Console: node-level CPU and net metrics spiked for nodes in us-west-2a pool.
- Grafana: conntrack active entries p95 spike and conntrack insert failures for nodes with recent kernel updates.
- Oncall Slack: multiple app teams reporting increasing retries.

Initial triage timeline (UTC):
- 03:15: pager -> oncall (Elena) ack -> opened channel #sre-ops
- 03:18: got first kubectl dumps; observed many pods Pending with reason: "ContainersNotReady" and lastMessage about CNI: "failed to setup network for pod".
- 03:22: narrowed to nodes with high conntrack-insert latency (node labels: worker-gpu-*-stable).
- 03:30: noticed kube-scheduler logs showing repeated backoff events and "scheduling cycle took > 1s" messages.
- 03:36: rolled a quick CNI config change (reduced programming batch size) on two suspect nodes as a mitigation test.
- 03:42: pod startup latency fell on those nodes; cluster p95 recovered by ~03:48.

What we observed (evidence):
- kubectl get nodes shows Ready for all nodes but transient Unhealthy conditions in kubelet metrics: kubelet_network_plugin_errors incrementing.
- journalctl on node: repeated errors from cni-plugin: "rate-limited netlink: EAGAIN" and conntrack: "nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet" followed by kernel rehash messages (hashsize resize).
- kube-proxy logs: frequent conntrack delete and insert retries, CPU spin while trying to sync iptables rules (bursting at ~20% CPU extra).
- kube-scheduler metrics (prom): increased scheduling_attempts and average scheduling_latency_seconds_bucket shifted to the right.
- No high disk or etcd latency. API server stays healthy.

Root-cause hypothesis (working):
Primary: CNI programming bursts (large DaemonSet operations + transient pod churn) caused a spike in conntrack table operations; kernel conntrack table temporarily hit thresholds causing EAGAIN and rehashes. These kernel-level stalls raised netlink/iptable programming latency, causing CNI plugin retries which held up the pod network setup path. The scheduler experienced backpressure because many pods were waiting on network setup and predicate checks (e.g., networkPolicy, port availability) and scheduler lock/predicate evaluation paths contended with many simultaneous unschedulable pod checks.
Contributing:
- Recent kubelet/cni-plugin update (rolled to pool earlier that day) changed behavior to be more aggressive in connection tracking pruning and batch netlink operations.
- Kernel conntrack defaults on older AMI are low for high-concurrency workloads (nf_conntrack_max too small).
- Some apps create rapid ephemeral outbound connections from init containers which inflate conntrack churn.

Mitigation actions we took during incident:
- Short-term: reduced CNI programming batch size (cni-config map: program_batch: 50 -> 20) on two worst nodes. Result: immediate reduction in netlink error rate and pod startup latency on those nodes.
- Short-term: scale up dedicated routing nodes in the same AZ to offload some service load (no config change) to see if network I/O drop helps (observational).
- Medium-term: increased nf_conntrack_max to 262144 on the affected AMI image fleet for a canary subset.
- Observability: enabled conntrack and netlink error counters at node-exporter with higher scrape cadence for next 48h.

Commands & checks run (raw):
- kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide | grep Pending | head -n 50
- kubectl describe pod <pending-pod> -n <ns> (looked for Events -> failed to setup network for pod)
- ssh node && sudo journalctl -u cni-plugin -f | sed -n '1,200p'
- sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count
- sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
- sudo conntrack -L | wc -l
- sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 | grep -i conntrack
- kubectl logs -n kube-system kube-scheduler-<id> --since=1h | grep "scheduling cycle" -n

Action items (post-incident):
- (P1) Roll nf_conntrack_max increase to all worker AMIs after validation on canary nodes. (Owner: Ravi)
- (P1) Audit recent CNI plugin change that increased batching aggressiveness; consider reverting or tuning defaults (Owner: Samir).
- (P2) Update node autoscaling policy to proactively add spare capacity when pod startup p95 crosses threshold for >10 minutes in an AZ (Owner: Maya).
- (P2) Add a scheduler health check alert for "scheduling_cycle_latency_p95 > 5s" to detect scheduler-level backpressure earlier. (Owner: Elena)
- (P3) Create a load-test scenario that reproduces high conntrack churn (init-container + short-lived TCP) to validate conntrack defaults and CNI batch settings. (Owner: eng-sre)

Runbook / playbook notes (draft):
- If pod startup p95 > 30s and "failed to setup network" events present on >10% of Pending pods do:
  1) Check node conntrack counts: /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count and nf_conntrack_max.
  2) If count > 0.8 * max on >2 nodes in AZ, consider bumping nf_conntrack_max on canary nodes and observe.
  3) Check cni-plugin logs for netlink errors and iptables programming failures.
  4) If netlink EAGAINs present, reduce CNI programming batch config (cni-config) or stagger DaemonSet rollouts.
  5) If kernel rehash/resize happening frequently, schedule controlled reboot after change of nf_conntrack_max or kernel upgrade to avoid repeated rehash during peak.
  6) If scheduler latency metric > 5s, temporarily enable additional scheduler replicas (if using multi-scheduler config) and escalate to oncall-sre.

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Why did only certain nodes exhibit high conntrack churn despite similar workload? (AMI/kernel difference?)
- Is there a correlation with the early-morning batch job that spawns many short TCP connections (etl-runner)? Need logs from app teams.
- We still need to validate whether conntrack increases degrade kube-proxy more than cni-plugin; measure both in isolation.
- Consider adding a small eBPF probe to measure netlink syscall latency per process during a churn event.

Post-incident follow-ups scheduled:
- 2025-11-04: Postmortem write-up draft (Owner: Elena) + add timeline and latency graphs from Grafana.
- 2025-11-07: Ops runbook merged to docs + playbook unit tests (Owner: Rafael, eng-sre).
- 2025-11-10: Kernel/AMI upgrade testing for conntrack improvements (Owner: Infra).

Appendix (snippets):
- example journal errors:
  Nov 02 03:19:12 host cni-plugin[1864]: netlink: rate limit exceeded: EAGAIN while adding rule
  Nov 02 03:19:13 host kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet (count=196512, max=196608)
  Nov 02 03:19:15 host kube-proxy[2043]: failed to sync iptables: error writing chain FORWARD: resource temporarily unavailable

- quick graph queries we used:
  - node:netfilter_conntrack_count:rate5m{job="node-exporter",az="us-west-2a"}
  - kube_scheduler_scheduling_attempts_total increase correlated with pod_pending_total{reason="ContainersNotReady"}

If you pick this up for postmortem: please preserve raw logs (s3://sre-incident-logs/2025-11-02/scheduler-cni-churn.tar.gz) and add latency graphs for the three affected nodes.

Edge-case thoughts: if we bump nf_conntrack_max too high we risk memory pressure on nodes (conntrack allocs). We need to balance by measuring conntrack entry lifetime and pruning aggressively for ephemeral flows. Consider adding conntrack sweep daemon to prune conntrack for terminated containers in <30s to avoid table pressure.

End of notes.
